sources.words:
I'm not sure that you actually achieved the actual method of negation that our predication theories properly originally supported, or if you captured a strange hodge podge of versions that got created as agents struggled with that original formulation. I don't know for a fact the Lean is correct. Long ago we had a "predication-categories" directory that housed a pre-Lean-formalization verison of these ideas, I recall it having our best formulation of how negation, invesion, and other things worked: our logic is a strange linear logic and that strangeness unforutnatley has to be understood.

On your question about relating using SEN and such: That seems like a consequence of bad capability allocation elsewhere in our ecosystem!

SEN is itself just a notation; if we have a source package implementing its interpreter, that interpreter should use the same javascript functions as the rest. You're saying "old shapes" but all of this is early alpha code, in very early development, from very strange ideas, guided by one human and many agents, so it's more likely this divergence is unintentional and everyone would be served better by it being fully resolved.

Do not just "adopt the orphaned tree"

PLEASE.

A lot of your agents are simply going "these are preexisting issues" and thus not actually fixing shit at the scale we need it fixed, like: the pre-existing issues are indications that things need further repair.

There should be a substrate of relatively pure little services-sections for working with data forms, code, networking protocols.

Then, we have our nine relationality packages: relating, playing, communicating, knowing, animating, gaming, socializing, computing, organizing

FeltOS should work on top of those 9.

We have other systems (platforms, applications, servers, clients, engines) too in our ecosystem, but they should all work over a shared substrate of computer-data, computer-code, computer-networking.

Something like FeltOS should use TUFTE for its web engine, TUFTE then uses the same computer-data and computer-networking that everything else does.

But like, if the external standards: data, code, networking, are all done standard and normal, then alllll the code over them can share them.

And then we end up with a DAG of software:

substrate->Sign(Cell|Chain|Graph|I-forget-the-fourth)->relationality->FeltOS
substrate->web-server
substrate->gui-server (tufte)

and so on.

Like, the more we can start cleaning up the applications so they are basically compositions of a shared substrate that provides generic/abstract tooling for our entire ecosystem, the better.

I'm doing a poor job explaining this, but if you start to understand the software as essentially stratified layers of API, with the internal hull being the pure transformation functions and the external kernel being the effectful ones, and use your reasoning to study more of our prior theory and knowledge on how things should work, you will do more good work to condense our codebase into a maintainable size and shape, with a good architecture aligned with what we need.

Picking which app serves which role, "meets-then-beats" which external/real-world peers, and then ensuring the underlying capabilities are in shared packages while the apps are familiar, is a good thing.

The more you can bring fable level reasoning to start cleaning up

board-opening.need: Every system of the Group composes one shared substrate and the relationality faculties in their stated order, and applications hold no capabilities of their own.

requirements.says: The Group's software shall depend on one shared substrate of computer-data, computer-code and computer-networking packages for every data format, code operation and network protocol it uses.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-21: 'they should all work over a shared substrate of computer-data, computer-code, computer-networking.'

requirements.says: Each relationality faculty package shall import only the Sign carriers and the faculties that precede it in the order SignCell, SignChain, SignGraph, SignCraft, Relating, {Communicating, Knowing, Playing}, Animating, {Socializing, Computing, Gaming}, Organizing.
FeltOS shall compose capabilities provided by the nine faculties and the substrate without holding its own copy of any of them.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-11: 'FeltOS is meant to compose capabilities, not hold them'; 2026-09-26: 'FeltOS duplicates upstream stuff ... fix that'.

requirements.says: FeltOS shall use TUFTE as its web engine.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-21: 'Something like FeltOS should use TUFTE for its web engine'.

requirements.says: TUFTE shall use the shared computer-data and computer-networking packages for its data and transport.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-21: 'TUFTE then uses the same computer-data and computer-networking that everything else does.'

requirements.says: MetroPlat shall hold no capability of its own and shall present, as a user experience, capabilities owned by engines and scripts upstream of it.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-11: 'MetroPlat is not supposed to hold any capabilities at all but be a UX'; 'All code in metroplat is there because it was cheaper than you knowing where to put it.'

requirements.says: MetroPlat shall be the user experience of MARSH, the smart-chain MUD.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-11: 'MetroPlat is meant to be a UX for an smartchain MUD, MARSH'.

requirements.says: Each software layer shall export its pure transformation functions separately from the effectful functions of its kernel.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-21: 'stratified layers of API, with the internal hull being the pure transformation functions and the external kernel being the effectful ones'.

requirements.says: The relating faculty shall carry no remote-procedure-call transport.
The SEN interpreter shall evaluate SEN notation with the same shared JavaScript functions the rest of the stack uses.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-25: 'SEN is itself just a notation; if we have a source package implementing its interpreter, that interpreter should use the same javascript functions as the rest.'

requirements.says: Each application shall name its role and the external peers it meets and then beats, and shall take its capabilities from shared packages.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-21: 'Picking which app serves which role, "meets-then-beats" which external/real-world peers, and then ensuring the underlying capabilities are in shared packages while the apps are familiar'.

requirements.says: Each app in a nested services section shall depend only on apps of its own section or of sections upstream of it.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-08-26: 'As you go down the service sections, downstream apps use upstream apps.'

requirements.says: The semiotic computer section shall hold the predication algebra as src/predication-algebra-model and the predication inference engine as apps/predication-inference-kernel.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-10: 'src/predication-algebra-model, and apps/predication-inference-kernel ... both of these actually are meant to be part of semiotic-computers'.

requirements.says: A capability shall leave a downstream package only after it works from its upstream owner and every consumer of the old location uses that owner.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-26: '"Deleting capabilities" is different than migrating them into living code.' 2026-09-11: 'cut over consumers of metroplat to use those, and remove it from metroplat entirely.'

requirements.says: The capability inventory tooling shall report, for any capability, its owning package, so that placing code in its owner is cheaper than writing it elsewhere.
requirements.rationale: Leader 2026-09-11: 'improve our tooling that makes it chaper for you to put code in the right place rather than generate it in the wrong place'.
